do_not_repeat: 2 KiB chunks: 48x4-byte handles do not fit the 128-byte context slot
Copy-based regrow of the final chunk: fragments RAM (picker loses 4-page blocks) and costs ~129 B
Largest-run partial chunk: starves the picker cache
Sweep must not fill optional choice options (None = base config, e.g. no REU)
Sampling N_READY on hardware a fixed 60 s after reset: GEMDESK first publishes ready ~111 s after reset (the 0/300 readings were my error)
Raw-stepping a pointer app's CPU model outside the harness: without simulated raster the code busy-waits; measure through the harness (frame())
Tick-only AES idle wait: the 1351 read is two-phase (start in raster 80..159, finish 32 lines later); the wait must drive pm_poll
Bytes saved before GEMDESK's .align 256 become padding; place code before the align to use the slack

performance_analysis.cost: ~65 instructions per transferred byte (transfer loop + heap_far_store php/sei/zp save + KERNAL INDSTA gateway) plus heap_check_record walking EVERY page of the allocation per transfer.
performance_analysis.measured_gemdesk: Idle GEMDESK frame through the harness: ~2,300 instructions (about 1,100 per AES sample).
performance_analysis.rejected: Widening bottom common RAM to 16K so N_BUFFER ($3a00) is visible in both banks: bank-1 allocations start at page $04, so $0400-$3fff bank-1 transfers would hit bank 0 (corruption).
options: copy loop in bottom-1K common RAM toggling $ff00 per byte (~25 cycles/byte, needs free common RAM + IRQ policy decision)
validate only touched pages per transfer (contract: 'each transfer checks page tags' - decide scope)
hoist zp/pointer save out of the per-byte path while keeping per-byte IRQ windows
performance_analysis.constraints: resident kernel ~6 bytes free; kernel docs promise IRQs run between bytes; any change needs the full sweep + VICE + hardware
